text.text_excerpt: Hell to the yes. Saffron Nola was awesome. I went with zero expectations. Shari V set up everything, so Saffron completely flew under my radar. This restaurant is functioning at a high level and has fantastic food. Oyster bed roast was our starter. The oysters were topped with onions and garlic. Nice balance of seasoning. It was served with the house naan. The naan is a topic on it's own. Light and airy with a buttery taste. This bread was one of my favorite parts about the meal. We made sure we had a steady steam of naan for all courses. After oysters, we had a threesome of saag, eggplant and gobi (cauliflower) served in small portions and eaten with roti. My sweetheart made reservations for our anniversary dinner for Wednesday at 8pm. To be extra sure they had our reservation, he called the morning of to confirm our table for 2. We arrived at 7:55pm, and were told that since we were early, we could hang out at the bar. The bar seating was at capacity so we kinda just hung out at the corner of the bar. We were given drink menus to peruse but no one took our order; when two seats opened up, we claimed them quickly. Once we were seated, we were greeted by a bartender--I ordered the French rose, and P ordered a "New Kid on the Block". Yall, the tamarind (?) that they burn atop the glass smells HEAVENLY! Absolutely loved our dinner here! One of our favorite spots in NOLA, and we try to hit all the top restaurants here (new and old) when we come. Fantastic drinks, fantastic service, and fantastic food. I love how they add an Indian flare to classics like the Old Fashioned, the seafood gumbo, and the flan. Our favorites were the apps: Bombay shrimp and chicken lasooni. The shrimp was probably one of my favorite shrimp preparations I've ever had, and that chicken flavor was perfect! The garlic naan was absolutely heavenly and we kept ordering more. The goat masala was pretty bomb too. My only criticism would be to add some more spice level.
